audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Sabbath controversies, mercy not sacrifice, servant citation, spirit-language controversy, blasphemy warning, tree/fruit, sign of Jonah, return of unclean spirit, and redefinition of family around doing the Father's will.

verses.restored: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath; his disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and eat.

familiar.text: At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.

modern.text: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began to pick the heads of grain and eat them.

original.text: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἐπορεύθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς σάββασιν διὰ τῶν σπορίμων· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπείνασαν καὶ ἤρξαντο τίλλειν στάχυας καὶ ἐσθίειν.

verses.restored: The Pharisees saw and said to him, Look, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.

familiar.text: But when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day.

modern.text: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to Him, “Look, Your disciples are doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἰδόντες εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ οἱ μαθηταί σου ποιοῦσιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ποιεῖν ἐν σαββάτῳ.

verses.restored: He said to them, Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those with him,

familiar.text: But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;

modern.text: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε ⸀ἐπείνασεν καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ;

verses.restored: how he entered the house of the Divine and ate the bread of the Presence, which was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests?

familiar.text: How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?

modern.text: He entered the house of God, and he and his companions ate the consecrated bread, which was not lawful for them to eat, but only for the priests.

original.text: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ⸂ἔφαγον, ὃ⸃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἦν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν οὐδὲ τοῖς μετʼ αὐτοῦ, εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν μόνοις;

verses.restored: Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?

familiar.text: Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?

modern.text: Or haven’t you read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and yet are innocent?

original.text: ἢ οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι τοῖς σάββασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τὸ σάββατον βεβηλοῦσιν καὶ ἀναίτιοί εἰσιν;

verses.restored: But I say to you: something greater than the temple is here.

familiar.text: But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.

modern.text: But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.

original.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῦ ἱεροῦ μεῖζόν ἐστιν ὧδε.

verses.restored: If you had known what this means, I desire mercy and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the guiltless.

familiar.text: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.

modern.text: If only you had known the meaning of ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the innocent.

original.text: εἰ δὲ ἐγνώκειτε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν, οὐκ ἂν κατεδικάσατε τοὺς ἀναιτίους.

verses.restored: For the Son of Humanity is lord of the Sabbath.

familiar.text: For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.

modern.text: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.” Jesus Heals on the Sabbath (Mark 3:1–6; Luke 6:6–11)

original.text: κύριος γάρ ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

verses.restored: Departing from there, he came into their synagogue.

familiar.text: And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:

modern.text: Moving on from there, Jesus entered their synagogue,

original.text: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτῶν·

verses.restored: And look, there was a man with a withered hand. They asked him, Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath? so that they might accuse him.

familiar.text: And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.

modern.text: and a man with a withered hand was there. In order to accuse Jesus, they asked Him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ⸀ἄνθρωπος χεῖρα ἔχων ξηράν. καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Εἰ ἔξεστι τοῖς σάββασιν ⸀θεραπεύειν; ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He said to them, What person among you who has one sheep, if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?

modern.text: He replied, “If one of you has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will he not take hold of it and lift it out?

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τίς ⸀ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἕξει πρόβατον ἕν, καὶ ἐὰν ἐμπέσῃ τοῦτο τοῖς σάββασιν εἰς βόθυνον, οὐχὶ κρατήσει αὐτὸ καὶ ἐγερεῖ;

verses.restored: How much more valuable is a human than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.

familiar.text: How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

modern.text: How much more valuable is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”

original.text: πόσῳ οὖν διαφέρει ἄνθρωπος προβάτου. ὥστε ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν καλῶς ποιεῖν.

verses.restored: Then he said to the man, Stretch out your hand. He stretched it out, and it was restored healthy like the other.

familiar.text: Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like as the other.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored to full use, just like the other.

original.text: τότε λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· Ἔκτεινόν ⸂σου τὴν χεῖρα⸃· καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη.

verses.restored: But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.

familiar.text: Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.

modern.text: But the Pharisees went out and plotted how they might kill Jesus. God’s Chosen Servant (Isaiah 42:1–9)

original.text: ⸂ἐξελθόντες δὲ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον κατʼ αὐτοῦ⸃ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.

verses.restored: Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from there. Many followed him, and he healed them all,

familiar.text: But when Jesus knew it, he withdrew himself from thence: and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them all;

modern.text: Aware of this, Jesus withdrew from that place. Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them all,

original.text: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς γνοὺς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν. καὶ ἠκολούθησαν ⸀αὐτῷ πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς πάντας,

verses.restored: and warned them that they should not make him known,

familiar.text: And charged them that they should not make him known:

modern.text: warning them not to make Him known.

original.text: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ φανερὸν αὐτὸν ποιήσωσιν,

verses.restored: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:

familiar.text: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,

modern.text: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:

original.text: ⸀ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·

verses.restored: Look, my servant whom I chose, my beloved in whom my soul delights; I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will announce justice to the nations.

familiar.text: Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

modern.text: “Here is My Servant, whom I have chosen, My beloved, in whom My soul delights. I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will proclaim justice to the nations.

original.text: Ἰδοὺ ὁ παῖς μου ὃν ᾑρέτισα, ὁ ἀγαπητός μου ⸂εἰς ὃν⸃ εὐδόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· θήσω τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπʼ αὐτόν, καὶ κρίσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπαγγελεῖ.

verses.restored: He will not quarrel or cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets.

familiar.text: He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets.

modern.text: He will not quarrel or cry out; no one will hear His voice in the streets.

original.text: οὐκ ἐρίσει οὐδὲ κραυγάσει, οὐδὲ ἀκούσει τις ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not quench, until he brings justice to victory.

familiar.text: A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.

modern.text: A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish, till He leads justice to victory.

original.text: κάλαμον συντετριμμένον οὐ κατεάξει καὶ λίνον τυφόμενον οὐ σβέσει, ἕως ἂν ἐκβάλῃ εἰς νῖκος τὴν κρίσιν.

verses.restored: And in his name the nations will hope.

familiar.text: And in his name shall the Gentiles trust.

modern.text: In His name the nations will put their hope.” A House Divided (Mark 3:20–27; Luke 11:14–23)

original.text: καὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν.

verses.restored: Then they brought to him a person troubled by an unclean spirit, blind and mute; and he healed him, so that the mute person spoke and saw.

familiar.text: Then was brought unto him one possessed with a devil, blind, and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw.

modern.text: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to Jesus, and He healed the man so that he could speak and see.

original.text: Τότε ⸂προσηνέχθη αὐτῷ δαιμονιζόμενος τυφλὸς καὶ κωφός⸃· καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτόν, ὥστε τὸν ⸀κωφὸν λαλεῖν καὶ βλέπειν.

verses.restored: All the crowds were amazed and said, Can this be the Son of David?

familiar.text: And all the people were amazed, and said, Is not this the son of David?

modern.text: The crowds were astounded and asked, “Could this be the Son of David?”

original.text: καὶ ἐξίσταντο πάντες οἱ ὄχλοι καὶ ἔλεγον· Μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς Δαυίδ;

verses.restored: But the Pharisees heard and said, This one does not cast out unclean spirits except by Beelzebul, ruler of those spirits.

familiar.text: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils.

modern.text: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “Only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, does this man drive out demons.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες εἶπον· Οὗτος οὐκ ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ Βεελζεβοὺλ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων.

verses.restored: Knowing their thoughts, he said to them, Every reign divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.

familiar.text: And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand:

modern.text: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and every city or household divided against itself will not stand.

original.text: εἰδὼς ⸀δὲ τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία μερισθεῖσα καθʼ ἑαυτῆς ἐρημοῦται, καὶ πᾶσα πόλις ἢ οἰκία μερισθεῖσα καθʼ ἑαυτῆς οὐ σταθήσεται.

verses.restored: If Satan/adversary casts out Satan/adversary, he is divided against himself; how then will his reign stand?

familiar.text: And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand?

modern.text: If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then can his kingdom stand?

original.text: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς τὸν Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλει, ἐφʼ ἑαυτὸν ἐμερίσθη· πῶς οὖν σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ;

verses.restored: If I by Beelzebul cast out unclean spirits, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.

familiar.text: And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.

modern.text: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.

original.text: καὶ εἰ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ⸂κριταὶ ἔσονται ὑμῶν⸃.

verses.restored: But if I by Spirit of the Divine cast out unclean spirits, then the reign of the Divine has come upon you.

familiar.text: But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.

modern.text: But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

original.text: εἰ δὲ ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Or how can someone enter the house of the strong one and seize his goods unless he first binds the strong one? Then he will plunder his house.

familiar.text: Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.

modern.text: Or again, how can anyone enter a strong man’s house and steal his possessions, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can plunder his house.

original.text: ἢ πῶς δύναταί τις εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ⸀ἁρπάσαι, ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον δήσῃ τὸν ἰσχυρόν; καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ ⸀διαρπάσει.

verses.restored: The one not with me is against me, and the one not gathering with me scatters.

familiar.text: He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.

modern.text: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters. The Unpardonable Sin (Mark 3:28–30)

original.text: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετʼ ἐμοῦ κατʼ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετʼ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.

verses.restored: Because of this I say to you: every sin/misalignment and blasphemy will be released for people, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be released.

familiar.text: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.

modern.text: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πᾶσα ἁμαρτία καὶ βλασφημία ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, ἡ δὲ τοῦ πνεύματος βλασφημία οὐκ ⸀ἀφεθήσεται.

verses.restored: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Humanity, it will be released for him; but whoever speaks against the holy Spirit, it will not be released, neither in this age nor in the coming one.

familiar.text: And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.

modern.text: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come. Good and Bad Fruit (Luke 6:43–45)

original.text: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν εἴπῃ λόγον κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ· ὃς δʼ ἂν εἴπῃ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ οὔτε ἐν ⸂τούτῳ τῷ⸃ αἰῶνι οὔτε ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι.

verses.restored: Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for from the fruit the tree is known.

familiar.text: Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit.

modern.text: Make a tree good and its fruit will be good, or make a tree bad and its fruit will be bad; for a tree is known by its fruit.

original.text: Ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον καλὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ καλόν, ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον σαπρὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ σαπρόν· ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ καρποῦ τὸ δένδρον γινώσκεται.

verses.restored: Offspring of vipers, how can you speak good things while being harmful? For from the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

familiar.text: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

modern.text: You brood of vipers, how can you who are evil say anything good? For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.

original.text: γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς δύνασθε ἀγαθὰ λαλεῖν πονηροὶ ὄντες; ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας τὸ στόμα λαλεῖ.

verses.restored: The good person brings out good things from the good treasure, and the harmful person brings out harmful things from the harmful treasure.

familiar.text: A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.

modern.text: The good man brings good things out of his good store of treasure, and the evil man brings evil things out of his evil store of treasure.

original.text: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει ἀγαθά, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει πονηρά.

verses.restored: I say to you that every idle word people speak, they will give an account for it in the day of judgment.

familiar.text: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.

modern.text: But I tell you that men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken.

original.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ ⸀λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως·

verses.restored: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.

familiar.text: For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.

modern.text: For by your words you will be acquitted, and by your words you will be condemned.” The Sign of Jonah (Jonah 3:1–10; Luke 11:29–32)

original.text: ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.

verses.restored: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.

familiar.text: Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee.

modern.text: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees said to Him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.”

original.text: Τότε ἀπεκρίθησαν ⸀αὐτῷ τινες τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἀπὸ σοῦ σημεῖον ἰδεῖν.

verses.restored: He answered them, A harmful and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.

familiar.text: But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas:

modern.text: Jesus replied, “A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ τοῦ προφήτου.

verses.restored: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-creature three days and three nights, so the Son of Humanity will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.

familiar.text: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

modern.text: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

original.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἦν Ἰωνᾶς ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ τοῦ κήτους τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας, οὕτως ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ τῆς γῆς τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας.

verses.restored: Men of Nineveh will rise in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they turned/realigned at the proclamation of Jonah; and look, something greater than Jonah is here.

familiar.text: The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

modern.text: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.

original.text: ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.

verses.restored: The queen of the South will rise in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom; and look, something greater than Solomon is here.

familiar.text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

modern.text: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here. An Unclean Spirit Returns (Luke 11:24–26)

original.text: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτήν· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.

verses.restored: When an unclean spirit goes out from a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest and does not find it.

familiar.text: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none.

modern.text: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it.

original.text: Ὅταν δὲ τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται διʼ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκει.

verses.restored: Then it says, I will return to my house from which I came. Coming, it finds it empty, swept, and put in order.

familiar.text: Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.

modern.text: Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’ On its return, it finds the house vacant, swept clean, and put in order.

original.text: τότε λέγει· ⸂Εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ἐπιστρέψω⸃ ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον· καὶ ἐλθὸν ⸀εὑρίσκει ⸀σχολάζοντα σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.

verses.restored: Then it goes and takes with itself seven other spirits more harmful than itself, and entering, they dwell there; and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first. So it will be also with this harmful generation.

familiar.text: Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.

modern.text: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there; and the final plight of that man is worse than the first. So will it be with this wicked generation.” Jesus’ Mother and Brothers (Mark 3:31–35; Luke 8:19–21)

original.text: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει μεθʼ ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτὰ ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ· καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων. οὕτως ἔσται καὶ τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ πονηρᾷ.

verses.restored: While he was still speaking to the crowds, look, his mother and brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.

familiar.text: While he yet talked to the people, behold, his mother and his brethren stood without, desiring to speak with him.

modern.text: While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, His mother and brothers stood outside, wanting to speak to Him.

original.text: Ἔτι ⸀δὲ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος τοῖς ὄχλοις ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ εἱστήκεισαν ἔξω ζητοῦντες αὐτῷ λαλῆσαι.

verses.restored: Someone said to him, Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak to you.

familiar.text: Then one said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to speak with thee.

modern.text: Someone told Him, “Look, Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak to You.”

original.text: ⸂εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἔξω ἑστήκασιν, ζητοῦντές σοι λαλῆσαι.⸃

verses.restored: He answered the one speaking to him, Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?

familiar.text: But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?

modern.text: But Jesus replied, “Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ ⸀λέγοντι αὐτῷ· Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου, καὶ τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ ἀδελφοί μου;

verses.restored: Stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said, Look, my mother and my brothers.

familiar.text: And he stretched forth his hand toward his disciples, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!

modern.text: Pointing to His disciples, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers.

original.text: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου·

verses.restored: For whoever does the will of my Father in the heavens is my brother and sister and mother.

familiar.text: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.

modern.text: For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.”

original.text: ὅστις γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, αὐτός μου ἀδελφὸς καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν.
